summary: Regression pass after XSS-sanitization code-review fixes (DOMPurify wrapper applied to all innerHTML / dangerouslySetInnerHTML sites; Python `is True/False` swapped for truthy checks; Dashboard refresh wrapped in useCallback). 43/43 backend tests PASS. All requested frontend flows PASS: text edit & save, sanitized rendering on reload, asset hover preview (640px wide), asset right-click context menu, PDF export, Dashboard list/navigation. Critical XSS storage check verified:
action_items: Non-blocking hardening (NOT a regression from this iter): CanvasBlock.jsx contenteditable has no onPaste handler. A user who pastes raw '' HTML from clipboard will see the onerror fire ONCE inside their own session before save/blur sanitises it (self-XSS, not stored XSS). Persisted DB content is already clean, so other viewers / reloads are safe. To fully neutralise the transient alert, add an onPaste handler that does `e.preventDefault(); document.execCommand('insertText', false, e.clipboardData.getData('text/plain'))` — or run sanitizeHtml on `text/html` before inserting. Low priority because (a) the requirement was 'content should be saved without the script tag / event handler' which is met, and (b) the threat model is self-XSS.

Editor.jsx is 1612 lines (was 1236 last iter, grew by ~376 for sanitize + features). Still over the 700-line guideline — recommend splitting into Toolbar / Canvas / Save+Export / TOC modules in a future refactor pass.
critical_code_review_comments: sanitize.js — ALLOWED_TAGS / ALLOWED_ATTR list is sensible (b,i,u,em,strong,p,br,span,div,ul,ol,li,a with style/class/href/target/rel/data-placeholder). FORBID_ATTR explicitly blocks onerror/onclick/onload/onmouseover/onfocus on top of DOMPurify's defaults. javascript: URLs in href are blocked by DOMPurify default policy. Good defence-in-depth.

sanitizeHtml is applied at every entry point: Editor.jsx chapter parsing (L443), fit-text probe (L670), onTextCommand save (L757), ExportPage dangerouslySetInnerHTML (L1307), PageThumbnail dangerouslySetInnerHTML (L1612); CanvasBlock.jsx useEffect (L35) and onBlur save (L145); LayersList.jsx plainTextSnippet (L80). No bypass paths spotted.
CanvasBlock.jsx contentEditable misses an onPaste handler — only stored content is sanitised, not the live editor state. Transient self-XSS possible during a paste event. Recommendation above.
Dashboard.jsx — refresh wrapped in useCallback as requested (verified rendering 8 cards on first visit, 2 cards after iter-10 test books were cleaned up). No stale-closure issues observed.
Backend test files no longer use `is True/False` comparisons (grep confirmed clean). All 43 pytest assertions still pass.
seed_data_creation: Created one transient text block 'HelloBold' on page 2 of book 664b1f40-e4d2-40df-874c-2b0ebe6ad645 during the XSS injection test, then deleted it via PUT /api/books/{id} at the end of the run. Book state is restored.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All XSS sanitization paths verified working at the storage layer. The one remaining transient-paste hole (no onPaste handler in CanvasBlock.jsx) is documented but considered out of scope for this code-review pass (the explicit requirement was 'content should be saved without script tag / event handler'). REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL must be exported when running pytest from CLI (otherwise test_assets_api / test_assets_book_scope_iter10 / test_page_number_align fail at module import with KeyError). Books in DB: 664b1f40... (The Incredible Journey of Money, 4 pages) and 6f8a91b5... (Friends in Every Color, 16 pages — slower for PDF export). PDF export for the 4-page book completed in 85s on this run.
rca of the issue: n/a — no regression introduced by the sanitize patch. Storage-layer XSS protection is complete: payload `HelloBold` inserted programmatically into a text block was saved to MongoDB as exactly `HelloBold`, and reload of the book caused zero alert dialogs. The single alert observed during the test fires inside the live contentEditable when execCommand inserts the raw before onBlur sanitises — this is self-XSS within the editing user's own session and does not persist.
